Use case: identity-preserve. Whole-creature game animation, fourteen complete tiny ground larvae.
Use the input as the cream/pink segmented body identity. Draw each larva with ONE circular dark red feeding opening at the HEAD, and a smooth CLOSED cream rounded REAR with no dark marking. The rounded rear must look like the closed end of a maggot. Keep soft underside folds as flesh, not feet. No legs.
Output exactly TWO ROWS with SEVEN figures in each row on a wide transparent atlas. Top row: ALL heads and their single feeding opening at the LEFT end, closed cream rear RIGHT. Bottom row: ALL heads and single feeding opening RIGHT, closed cream rear LEFT.
In each row, pose1 is stable idle; poses2..7 are six compact successive crawling contractions, not rotations. Head and rear never exchange places within a row. Low horizontal body, subtle traveling segment compression, constant body volume and scale. No upright body or raised tail.
Do not draw a second mouth, hole, dark oval, red socket or wound at the closed rear. No feet, claws or added appendages. No split body, floating pieces, glow, red halo or colored specks. Preserve pale body, dark brown clean contours, reddish single head opening and native64-readable matte game finish. Entire figures well inside generous transparent margins, no touching neighbors, no labels, grid, floor or shadow. Genuine alpha transparency.
